title: Papyrus Oracle Queries — Parallel Greek-English Edition
format: Oracle consultation texts with facing translations
organization: By consultation category and formula type

parallel_text.greek: Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι καὶ τοῖς συννάοις θεοῖς. ἀξιοῖ Εὔφορος, εἰ ἀνακτήσωμαι, τοῦτό μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, the Great Sarapis, and the gods who share the shrine.
parallel_text.note: “Zeus Helios the Great Sarapis” is a syncretic titulature identifying Sarapis with Zeus-Helios; συννάοις (“sharing the naos”) means ‘fellow-dwellers in the same shrine/temple.’

consultation_context.notes: Classic health consultation with full divine titulature

parallel_text.greek: [Διὶ Ἡ]λίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι [καὶ] τοῖς συννάοις [θε]οῖς. ἀξιοῖ Μένανδρος [εἰ] δέδοταί μοι γαμῆσαι. [τοῦ]το μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, to great Sarapis, and to the co-dwelling gods. Menandros asks whether it has been granted to me to marry. Grant me this.
parallel_text.note: The openings with bracketed letters are standard restorations: [Διὶ Ἡ]λίῳ (‘to Zeus Helios’), [καὶ] (‘and’), [θε]οῖς (‘gods’), [εἰ] introducing the indirect question, and [τοῦ]το (‘this’). The sequence of datives is a typical vocative/address formula in oracle petitions; it may list distinct recipients (Zeus Helios; great Sarapis; the synnaoi ‘co-dwelling’ gods), though some take ‘Zeus Helios, great Sarapis’ as a syncretic apposition. δέδοταί μοι is the conventional idiom for divine permission (‘it has been granted to me’). The switch from third person (‘Menandros asks’) to first person (‘to me’) is formulaic in such petitions. δός (‘grant/give’) takes τοῦτο elliptically (‘this [favor/answer]’).

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Is it granted me to marry?
consultation_context.notes: Classic marriage inquiry with δέδοται formula

parallel_text.greek: Διὶ Ἡλίωι Σαράπιδι Νικαφόρωι. εἰ ἐπιτρέπεις μοι χρήσασθαι Ἑρμείνωι Ἑρμοπολίτηι ἰατρῶι πρὸς θεραπείαν τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν, καὶ τοῦτό μοι συμφέρει, τοῦτό μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus-Helios Sarapis the Victory-bearer. If you permit me to consult Hermeinos the Hermopolite, a physician, for the treatment of the eyes, and this is to my advantage, grant me this.
parallel_text.note: Invocation in the dative (Διί Ἡλίῳ Σαράπιδι) is formulaic; the syncretic theonym Zeus‑Helios Sarapis is preserved, with the epithet Nikēphoros (‘Victory‑bearer’; papyrus spelling Νικαφόρωι). χρῆσθαι + dative = ‘to employ/consult’ (a professional). Ἑρμείνῳ Ἑρμοπολίτῃ ἰατρῷ are datives (with iota adscript in the papyrus). ‘For the treatment of the eyes’ is a set phrase; the possessor is implied. The conditional “if you permit … and it is expedient (συμφέρει) … grant me this (τοῦτο μοι δός)” is a standard oracular petition formula.

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Seeks permission to use Herminos (of Hermopolis) as a doctor for an eye condition.
consultation_context.notes: Detailed medical consultation with specific doctor and condition

parallel_text.greek: Κυρίῳ Σοκνοπαίῳ θεῷ μεγάλῳ καὶ Ἄμμωνι, θεοῖς μεγίστοις· ἀξιοῖ Σώτας, εἰ οὐ μέλλει ὁ νομάρχης ἐμαυτοῦ ἀγανακτεῖν ἢ ἐξετάζει τὰ κατ' ἐμέ, ὅτι τὰ πιττάκια Οὐαλερίου ἐγὼ γράφω, τοῦτό μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Lord Soknopaios, the great god, and to Ammon, the greatest gods: Sotas petitions—if the nomarch is not going to be angry with me or conduct an inquiry into my affairs, because I write the pittakia of Valerius, grant me this.
parallel_text.note: Soknopaios (Σοκνοπαίος) is the local Sobek; Ammon is the Greco-Egyptian Ammon. The plural apposition “θεοῖς μεγίστοις” is a formulaic epithet. ἀξιοῖ in papyri = “petitions.” Νομάρχης is rendered “nomarch” (a district/provincial official). ἀγανακτεῖν = “be vexed/indignant.” τὰ κατ᾿ ἐμέ = “matters concerning me.” πιττάκια (pittakia) are tickets/notes or official slips; left transliterated. τοῦτό μοι δός is the standard oracular ‘grant me this’ confirming an affirmative response.

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Asks whether the nomarch will be angry or examine him because he writes Valerius' pittakia.
consultation_context.notes: Workplace anxiety consultation - very human and relatable

parallel_text.greek: [Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι καὶ τοῖς συννάοις θεοῖς. ἀξιοῖ] Νίκη, εἰ συμφέρει αὐτῇ πρίασθαι Σαραπίωνα παῖδα παρὰ Τασαραπίωνος, [τοῦτό μοι δός].
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, the Great Sarapis, and the co-enshrined gods. Nike asks whether it is to her advantage to purchase Sarapion, a boy, from Tasarapion; grant me this.
parallel_text.note: Bracketed portions are standard restorations of the formula. Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι denotes the syncretic deity “Zeus Helios, the Great Sarapis”; τοῖς συννάοις θεοῖς = “the co‑enshrined gods.” ἀξιοῖ = “asks/requests”; εἰ συμφέρει = “whether it is advantageous/expedient.” πρίασθαι is middle “to purchase (as property).” παῖδα likely indicates a slave‑boy. παρὰ + gen. marks the seller (“from Tasarapion”).

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Asks if it is advantageous to buy a slave named Sarapion from Tasarapion.
consultation_context.notes: Business transaction consultation about slave purchase

parallel_text.greek: Σαράπιδι καὶ Ἴσιδι καὶ πᾶσι θεοῖς. ἀξιοῖ Διονύσιος τὸν θεὸν περὶ τῆς ἀσθενείας αὐτοῦ, εἰ συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἀπελθεῖν ἐπὶ τὰ ἴδια.
parallel_text.english: To Sarapis and Isis and all the gods. Dionysios petitions the god concerning his illness, whether it is expedient for him to go home.
parallel_text.note: The initial datives mark the formal address of an oracle query. ἀξιοῖ is a technical verb in petitions (‘to request/petition’). The singular τὸν θεόν after invoking multiple deities likely refers to the principal oracular deity (here Sarapis). ἐπὶ τὰ ἴδια is a papyrological idiom meaning ‘home’ (literally ‘to his own [things/places]’). συμφέρει carries the standard oracular nuance ‘is expedient/advantageous’.

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Consultation about illness and whether to return home
consultation_context.notes: Travel consultation related to health concerns

parallel_text.greek: Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι καὶ τοῖς συννάοις θεοῖς. περὶ γάμου. εἰ συμφέρει Διονυσίῳ γῆμαι Ἡραΐδα τὴν Ἡρακλείδου.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, the Great Sarapis, and the co-dwelling gods. Concerning marriage. Whether it is expedient for Dionysios to marry Heraïs, daughter of Herakleides.
parallel_text.note: The address formula identifies Zeus Helios with Sarapis in apposition (“Zeus Helios, the Great Sarapis”). συννάοις (‘co-dwelling’) refers to gods who share the same temple. περὶ γάμου functions as a docket “Concerning marriage.” εἰ here is best rendered “whether.” γῆμαι is the verb used of a man marrying. The genitive Ἡρακλείδου is dependent on an understood ‘daughter,’ hence “daughter of Herakleides.”

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Marriage consultation about specific bride candidate
consultation_context.notes: Specific marriage partner consultation with family details

parallel_text.greek: Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι. ἀξιοῖ Ἀπολλώνιος, εἰ συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἀντικαλεῖν Ἡρακλεῖδα περὶ τῶν ἐπικλήρων, τοῦτό μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, the great Sarapis. Apollonios requests: if it is to his advantage to bring a countersuit against Herakleidas concerning the epikleroi, grant me this.
parallel_text.note: “Zeus Helios, the great Sarapis” reflects a syncretic address to the deity; ἀξιοῖ = ‘requests’ in petition formulae; ἀντικαλεῖν is a legal term ‘to bring a counter-suit/countersummons’; ἐπίκληροι are ‘heiresses’ in Greek law; τοῦτό μοι δός is the oracular formula ‘grant me this [sign/answer].’

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Legal consultation about counter-suing in inheritance dispute
consultation_context.notes: Legal strategy consultation about inheritance litigation

parallel_text.greek: Διὶ Ἡλίῳ μεγάλῳ Σαράπιδι καὶ τοῖς συννάοις θεοῖς. ἀξιοῖ Ἡρακλείδης, εἰ συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἀναβῆναι εἰς Ἀλεξάνδρειαν πρὸς τὰ ἴδια πράγματα, τοῦτό μοι δός.
parallel_text.english: To Zeus Helios, to Great Sarapis, and to the co-dwelling gods. Herakleides petitions: if it is expedient for him to go up to Alexandria concerning his own affairs, grant me this.
parallel_text.note: Διὶ Ἡλίῳ … Σαράπιδι: a list of addressees, not apposition; Zeus Helios and Sarapis are invoked separately. συννάοις (“co-dwelling”) refers to gods sharing the same sanctuary. ἀξιοῖ is the standard petitionary formula in oracle-queries (“requests/petitions”). ἀναβῆναι (“go up”) is conventional for travel to a major center. πρὸς τὰ ἴδια πράγματα = “regarding his own affairs/private business.” τοῦτό μοι δός is the oracular formula “grant me this,” sc. a confirming sign/answer.

consultation_context.original_paraphrase: Travel consultation about business trip to Alexandria
consultation_context.notes: Business travel consultation to major city
